passage: The Ahmed Baba Institute in Timbuktu, Mali, holds tens of thousands of handwritten manuscripts on subjects ranging from law and medicine to astronomy and poetry. The institute takes its name from the sixteenth-century ______ Baba, who taught in Timbuktu and wrote dozens of works, many of them on Islamic law. Many of the institute's manuscripts were preserved for generations in private family libraries across the region.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The name "Ahmed Baba" tells which sixteenth-century scholar the institute is named for; without it, "the sixteenth-century scholar" would not identify anyone. Because the name is essential, it is not set off with punctuation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma would treat the name as extra information, but the name is essential to identify the scholar, so no comma belongs here.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, and neither side of this one is independent.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause, and "The institute takes its name from the sixteenth-century scholar" is not complete without the name.
explanation.D: Correct. No punctuation is used because the name "Ahmed Baba" is essential: it identifies which scholar is meant.
